# R410 — phase decode capacity and profile ranking options
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source/research review distinct from CPUkernelR409. Main's P/model diagnostic remained active and untouched. No source edit, build, test, lint, GPU/model, profiler, process/service query, cleanup, Git operation, or model-tensor read. Only this report was written.

## Finding

The implementation has a bounded capacity experiment worth testing, but no evidence yet that a larger cache improves decode hits or fits the model after prompt/head ownership is restored. The active configuration chooses 3 baseline slots plus 16 extras per layer: 19 x 48 = 912 resident slots at the decode boundary. `PhaseCacheOwner::reserve` permits `extras_per_layer` through 32, so the source-level upper candidate is 3+32=35/layer, 1,680 total. The hard limit is a parameter constraint, not a measured fit or hit-rate claim. Current code validates a complete 19-pair-per-layer static profile, selects its first 19 ranks, and fills rows 0–2 at startup, then rows 3–18 after prefill. A 24- or 32-extra candidate needs validation of all selected rows and corresponding profile rank before owner admission.

At prompt completion, `PhaseServeCycle::successful_prompt` runs workspace retirement, completes the prefill lease and baseline refill, reloads the native head, then maps/fills extras. `map_extras` performs a fresh actual free-memory admission after the baseline is mapped. It checks known free memory, unchanged VMM granularity/minimums, per-extent maximum allocation, total requested bytes against free bytes, and the 512 MiB guard. Each layer's extras are one VMM extent; a candidate must satisfy that extent's allocation maximum as well as the total free-memory guard. Thus the relevant observation is the actual free/max result at this boundary after all physical prefill cache/head ownership is restored. Startup or phase0 free samples cannot establish candidate fit. Reservation geometry also remains bounded by the current 8 GiB virtual cap and integer/address/alignment checks.

The active prefill route census already derives expert frequencies from the host-visible route IDs and counts them across each chunk/layer. It logs aggregate `active_experts` and nonresident counts, not the identities or ordering of the IDs. Those counts can describe whole-prompt popularity and reveal whether the configured static profile missed prompt mass; they cannot calculate sliding decode windows, temporal reuse, or per-layer cache hits. Existing data are available without a new GPU synchronization because the census runs after existing route handoff and completion, but telemetry emits aggregate counters only. A recent-prompt cache ranking would need a bounded per-layer frequency accumulator retaining expert identities, reset for every prompt, and must be labeled as prompt-derived. It will overfit unless evaluated against separate held-out requests. Do not turn attempted/prompt routes into emitted decode-token counts.

The earlier R369 v2 gives the correct packed-set arithmetic (one expert across 48 layers is 98,227,200 B; top-10 over all layers is 982,272,000 B) but explicitly has no current route overlap/cache hit measurement. R370 v2 describes safe route-observation seams and cautions that only completed/segmented paths qualify. Neither supplies evidence for this candidate's cache hit rate. R367's all-expert lease review says mapped-byte capacity is unchanged by lease design and that fresh physical fit must still be checked; it does not establish current P post-prefill headroom.

## Ranked options

1. **Keep the existing 19-rank/layer cache as control.** It is the only current P configuration described as qualified through tiny full-lease runtime; actual 1024/32768 remains active and not yet qualified. Preserve source profile bytes/hash and actual profile identity with each future result.
2. **Static 3+24/layer (1,296 slots), same profile ordering.** This is the smallest useful capacity increase. It requires a complete 27-rank/layer profile prefix and must pass the actual post-prefill map admission. This tests capacity under the current ranking without conflating ranking and size.
3. **Static 3+32/layer (1,680 slots), same profile ordering.** This is the owner-limit ceiling candidate, useful only if 24 fits and improves held-out decode hit opportunity. It has no source-level guarantee of map fit: each layer's 32-extra extent and whole-cache total must both pass fresh actual limits.
4. **Held-out static ranking variant, fixed at 3+16 or the largest admitted size.** Build the order from independent completed requests or a pre-existing validated profile; compare to the current profile on a disjoint request set. A per-layer prompt-frequency profile may be evaluated as a separate ranking arm, but training and evaluation prompts must be disjoint. Do not make it adaptive production state from the prompt being scored.
5. **Recent-window ranking is not ready.** It needs ordered token/layer route IDs and an explicit window/attempted-versus-committed definition. The current prompt aggregate is insufficient. R370's segmented decode callback is a candidate future observation point only where its documented completion conditions hold; the current active P route path must be confirmed against final source before implementation.

Do not combine size and ranking changes in one first comparison. Do not claim an arithmetic slot count predicts fit, hit rate, time saved, bandwidth, or 70 tok/s.

## Smallest useful stock-bench comparison, after active run closes and candidate is admitted

Use the unchanged stock bench client and one fixed request recipe: exact same prompt with at least 32,768 input tokens, same generation limit/sampling/seed where supported, same server settings and model/profile identity. Compare the existing 912-slot control against one capacity candidate first (1,296); only add 1,680 if 1,296 passes admission. Run at least three repetitions per arm in paired/interleaved order. Keep prefill and decode durations/results separate, record startup and prompt-to-decode lease/fill cost separately, and retain each run's route/cache logical counters, actual free/max admission evidence, quality/correctness outcome, and failure state. Repeat this matrix for a ranking candidate only after the size choice is fixed. Use identical client requests and report individual samples plus median and spread; do not compare phase0 free against post-prefill free or use raw route counters as physical bandwidth.

A ranking candidate should advance only if held-out decode routes show an improvement over the current profile in per-layer and byte-weighted opportunity, and the stock end-to-end measurements show no unacceptable prefill/lease cost or correctness/quality change. Decode GPU experts use FP16 activations while CPU experts use Q8, so placement can change rounding and generated text; exact text equality is not an appropriate gate. Preserve the current quality policy and report output variation. Cold-start, restore, full-256K context and full request lifecycle remain unqualified until separately exercised.
